_comment: GENERATED by api/src/scripts/measure-baseline.ts (PF-020). The denominator for the +10% regression budget on MVP gate item 9 (PRD p.2, targets p.6). Do not hand-edit — re-run the script. RE-CAPTURED 2026-08-13: the original run recorded absolute milliseconds that this machine no longer reproduces. Re-measuring the SAME baseline commit today gave 9.68/10.22/9.57/13.11 ms against recorded 3.63/3.99/3.69/4.24 — the baseline commit was 1.5-3x slower than its own recorded numbers, so the comparison was measuring the machine rather than the code. Query counts were identical throughout, which is what showed the difference was not extra work. This file's method note already says the measurement is 'a before/after pair, not a production SLO'; a pair is only a pair when both halves are taken under the same conditions, so the denominator is re-taken here in the same session as the numerator. Bundle bytes are unchanged (747644 gzip), which is the metric that does not depend on load.

method.transport: in-process (supertest), no TCP — a before/after pair, not a production SLO

budget.source: PRD p.2 (MVP gate item 9), p.6 (Performance Targets)

GET /health.note: Touches no database. The floor: middleware and routing only, so a regression here is a regression in the stack itself.

GET /api/documents.note: The flagship list endpoint and the one /api/v1/documents will mirror.

GET /api/documents/:id.note: Single-document read, the hottest shape in the UI.

GET /api/issues.note: Second list endpoint, different sort key (priority + updated_at).

GET /api/weeks.note: Sprints under their internal name; the public contract calls these sprints.

GET /api/dashboard/my-work.note: Read-only aggregate across documents, issues and memberships — the heaviest of the routine GETs, and the one an extra per-request query would show up on first.

_supersedes.note: Kept so the original numbers stay auditable rather than being silently overwritten.
